title: CA1 pyramidal-to-interneuron spike connections in 4 rats and 4 mice were nearly independent of place-map similarity, with at most a few percent per SD, less than in head-direction cortex
abstract: Question: in mouse postsubiculum, head-direction cells connect about 10% more often per SD of tuning similarity to fast-spiking interneurons. Does a like-to-like rule apply to place cells and interneurons in the hippocampus, and is it present before or only after a new maze? Data: DANDI:000044 (rat CA1, 4 rats, 8 sessions, each on a new maze) and DANDI:001695 (mouse CA1 and CA3, 4 mice, 14 sessions), both with rest before (PRE) and after (POST) the maze. Method: we detected putative pyramidal-to-interneuron connections with a cross-correlogram rule, separately for all, PRE, POST and NREM spikes. We modelled the connection rate against maze place-map similarity with one stratum for each interneuron. Synthetic connections of known strength added to all real pairs gave the pattern that tuning-blind wiring produces after detection. Results: we found 402 connections in 4,266 rat CA1 pairs and 2,768 in 32,034 mouse CA1 pairs; control pairs had 4 detections in 37,726. The rate ratio per SD of similarity was 0.93 (CI 0.86-1.03) in rat and 1.02 (1.00-1.05) in mouse. Injection nulls were 0.94-1.00. With one estimate for each of 8 CA1 animals, observed/null was 0.97 (0.88-1.07). The small mouse excess became 1.00 after we removed the spikes that the connection itself transmits. PRE-only detection before a new maze gave 0.98 (0.89-1.09) in rat. Mouse PRE gave 1.05 (0.99-1.09), and 1.06 (0.99-1.14) at the animal level. Transmission change from PRE to POST sleep did not depend on similarity. A mouse CA3 PRE-sleep excess did not hold at the animal level. Conclusion: CA1 excitatory input to interneurons is close to tuning-blind for place fields. Any like-to-like bias is at most a few percent per SD, smaller than the postsubicular head-direction value. Limitations: putative connections from spike timing, only strong connections, four animals per data set, repeated mouse sessions, no interneuron subtypes, and many secondary cuts without correction. Code, per-pair derived tables, figures and DANDI hashes are included; raw recordings stay external.

display.caption: Left: median-strength example cross-correlograms (blue) with the hollow-Gaussian baseline (orange); grey band is the 0.8-2.8 ms detection window. The rat example is a same-shank pair, so the dip near zero lag is a spike-sorting collision effect. Middle and right: percentage of pyramidal-to-interneuron pairs with a detected connection by place-map similarity decile, for all spikes and for PRE rest only. Blue: observed. Orange: tuning-blind synthetic-connection null (gain model, q50), scaled to the observed mean. Text: rate ratio per SD of similarity and observed/null ratio with session bootstrap CIs.

Rate ratio per SD of place-map similarity for connections detected with all spikes, PRE or POST rest spikes, and PRE or POST NREM spikes. Blue circles: observed. Orange squares: observed divided by the tuning-blind injection null (gain model). Bars: 95% session bootstrap CIs. Dotted line: the head-direction-to-FS value in mouse postsubiculum (1.10). n: number of detected connections.
